sections.heading: C — Emergency zones, parking rules, transporting loads and animals, ferries and beaches
sections.markdown:
## C — Emergency zones, parking rules, transporting loads and animals, ferries and beaches

FACT_ID: sec11-F01 | anchor: A143
Emergency zones may use flares or signs, but roadside response vehicles mark them with flashing lights. [A143]
Source: [A143 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0143]

FACT_ID: sec11-F02 | anchor: A143
When you see a roadside response vehicle with flashing lights you must either move into a lane farther away or slow to at least 10 mph under the posted limit. [A143]
Why it matters: the law gives two options, and slowing down is required when you cannot move over.
Source: [A143 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0143]

FACT_ID: sec11-F03 | anchor: A143
You must never go faster than 50 mph in an emergency zone. [A143]
Source: [A143 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0143]

FACT_ID: sec11-F04 | anchor: A143
Roadside response vehicles include tow trucks, garbage trucks, incident response, highway maintenance and utility vehicles as well as police, fire trucks and ambulances. [A143]
Source: [A143 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0143]

FACT_ID: sec11-F05 | anchor: A143
You are responsible for parking only in designated areas so your vehicle is not a hazard, and colored curbs can signal parking limits. [A143]
Source: [A143 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0143]

FACT_ID: sec11-F06 | anchor: A143
Never park in an intersection or on a crosswalk, a sidewalk or a bicycle lane. [A143]
Source: [A143 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0143]

FACT_ID: sec11-F07 | anchor: A143
Do not park within 30 feet of a traffic signal, a stop sign or a yield sign. [A143]
Source: [A143 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0143]

FACT_ID: sec11-F08 | anchor: A143
Do not park within 5 feet of a driveway, an alley or a private road. [A143]
Source: [A143 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0143]

FACT_ID: sec11-F09 | anchor: A143
Do not park within 75 feet of a fire station driveway when parking on the opposite side of the street. [A143]
Source: [A143 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0143]

FACT_ID: sec11-F10 | anchor: A144
Do not park within 20 feet of a pedestrian safety zone. [A144]
Source: [A144 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0144]

FACT_ID: sec11-F11 | anchor: A144
Never park on railroad tracks or within 50 feet of a railroad crossing. [A144]
Source: [A144 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0144]

FACT_ID: sec11-F12 | anchor: A144
Do not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant. [A144]
Why it matters: hydrant distance is the shortest of the fire-related limits; the fire station driveway limit is far longer.
Source: [A144 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0144]

FACT_ID: sec11-F13 | anchor: A144
A parked vehicle must face the same way as traffic and sit no more than 12 inches from the curb. [A144]
Source: [A144 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0144]

FACT_ID: sec11-F14 | anchor: A144
Parking is banned beside an already parked vehicle, in a construction zone, on a bridge, overpass, tunnel or underpass, and on a freeway shoulder except in an emergency. [A144]
Source: [A144 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0144]

FACT_ID: sec11-F15 | anchor: A144
A white painted curb allows only short stops, while a yellow or red curb marks a loading zone or another restriction. [A144]
Source: [A144 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0144]

FACT_ID: sec11-F16 | anchor: A144
Set the parking brake every time you park, and especially on a hill. [A144]
Source: [A144 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0144]

FACT_ID: sec11-F17 | anchor: A144
The Dutch Reach means checking your mirrors, then opening the door with the hand farthest from it, which turns your body so you see approaching cyclists. [A144]
Source: [A144 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0144]

FACT_ID: sec11-F18 | anchor: A145
Leaving a child younger than 16 alone in a parked vehicle with the motor running is a crime. [A145]
Source: [A145 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0145]

FACT_ID: sec11-F19 | anchor: A145
Leaving a child younger than 12 alone in a parked vehicle is a crime even with the motor off. [A145]
Why it matters: the higher age applies only when the engine is running.
Source: [A145 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0145]

FACT_ID: sec11-F20 | anchor: A145
Leaving an animal alone in a vehicle is a crime when heat, cold, poor ventilation or lack of water could injure or kill it. [A145]
Source: [A145 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0145]

FACT_ID: sec11-F21 | anchor: A145
If nobody nearby can open the vehicle, police may remove a child or animal by any reasonable means, and the officer or agency is not liable for the damage. [A145]
Source: [A145 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0145]

FACT_ID: sec11-F22 | anchor: A146
To pull into a perpendicular or angled space, check traffic, signal, creep forward while steering to the middle of the space, center between the lines, then stop and secure the vehicle. [A146]
Source: [A146 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0146]

FACT_ID: sec11-F23 | anchor: A146
To leave a perpendicular or angled space, back straight out while watching traffic until your bumper clears the next vehicle, then turn the wheel sharply the way you want to go. [A146]
Source: [A146 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0146]

FACT_ID: sec11-F24 | anchor: A147
To parallel park, back slowly until your front bumper lines up with the rear bumper of the car you are parking behind, then turn the wheel sharply and back in. [A147]
Source: [A147 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0147]

FACT_ID: sec11-F25 | anchor: A147
Stop before you touch the bumper of the vehicle behind you, then pull forward so you end up no more than 12 inches from the curb. [A147]
Source: [A147 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0147]

FACT_ID: sec11-F26 | anchor: A148
When leaving a parallel space, signal, steer forward slowly, and move into the nearest lane once your front door passes the rear bumper of the car ahead. [A148]
Source: [A148 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0148]

FACT_ID: sec11-F27 | anchor: A148
Facing uphill against a tall curb, turn the wheel away from the curb until the back of the front tire rests against it, so a rolling car stops at the curb. [A148]
Source: [A148 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0148]

FACT_ID: sec11-F28 | anchor: A148
Facing uphill with a low or rounded curb, turning the wheel toward the curb may be safer, because the car would then roll away from the road. [A148]
Source: [A148 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0148]

FACT_ID: sec11-F29 | anchor: A149
Facing downhill, turn the wheel toward the curb until the front of the front tire touches it. [A149]
Source: [A149 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0149]

FACT_ID: sec11-F30 | anchor: A149
On a hill with no curb, turn the wheels toward the road edge so the car rolls away from traffic. [A149]
Source: [A149 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0149]

FACT_ID: sec11-F31 | anchor: A149
The striped access aisle beside a disabled parking space must stay clear, and you can be fined for blocking it or parking there without the required placard. [A149]
Source: [A149 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0149]

FACT_ID: sec11-F32 | anchor: A149
A person whose disability limits or impairs walking may apply for temporary or permanent disabled parking by completing the application together with their physician. [A149]
Source: [A149 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0149]

FACT_ID: sec11-F33 | anchor: A150
Parking at an electric vehicle charging station is illegal unless your vehicle is plugged into the charger. [A150]
Source: [A150 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0150]

FACT_ID: sec11-F34 | anchor: A150
When towing a boat, trailer or camper you must follow manufacturer, state and federal rules on weight, hookups, brakes and licensing. [A150]
Source: [A150 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0150]

FACT_ID: sec11-F35 | anchor: A151
Driving with an unsecured load is illegal, so tie items down with rope, netting or straps and fasten large objects directly to the vehicle or trailer. [A151]
Source: [A151 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0151]

FACT_ID: sec11-F36 | anchor: A151
Carrying an animal outside the cab, such as in a truck bed, is illegal unless it is in a protective harness or enclosure. [A151]
Source: [A151 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0151]

FACT_ID: sec11-F37 | anchor: A151
Transporting an animal in a way that endangers it or the public is a misdemeanor under the state's animal cruelty laws. [A151]
Source: [A151 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0151]

FACT_ID: sec11-F38 | anchor: A151
A loose pet or one on the driver's lap is a distraction, and any activity that pulls focus from safe driving is illegal. [A151]
Source: [A151 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0151]

FACT_ID: sec11-F39 | anchor: A152
Washington State Ferries are part of the state highway network, so every rule of the road applies there. [A152]
Source: [A152 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0152]

FACT_ID: sec11-F40 | anchor: A152
Cutting into a ferry line is a traffic offense that can bring a fine, and a holding lane must not block home driveways or intersections. [A152]
Source: [A152 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0152]

FACT_ID: sec11-F41 | anchor: A152
Ocean beach driving is allowed only in Grays Harbor and Pacific counties, where the beach counts as a state highway. [A152]
Source: [A152 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0152]

FACT_ID: sec11-F42 | anchor: A152
On the beach the speed limit is 25 mph, and walkers and cyclists always have the right-of-way. [A152]
Source: [A152 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0152]

Glossary: roadside response vehicle — any vehicle working a roadside emergency with flashing lights [A143]. Double parking — stopping beside a car that is already parked [A144]. Dutch Reach — opening the door with the far hand [A144]. Access aisle — the striped space next to a disabled parking stall [A149]. Unsecured load — cargo not tied down [A151].
Memory aid: only uphill against a tall curb does the wheel turn away; downhill, a low curb uphill, or no curb, the wheel turns toward the curb or road edge [A148].
